title: Jeremiah's Call
summary: In the days of Josiah the word of the LORD comes to Jeremiah, son of a priest of Anathoth, saying he knew him before he formed him in the womb and appointed him a prophet to the nations. Jeremiah protests that he is only a child; the LORD touches his mouth and puts his words in it. He sees a branch of an almond tree and a boiling pot tilting from the north, and is told not to be afraid, for God will make him a fortified city.

title: The Potter's House and the Broken Jar
summary: The LORD sends Jeremiah to the potter's house, where a vessel marred in the potter's hand is made into another vessel, and says Israel is in his hand like clay. When the people reject the warning, Jeremiah is told to buy a clay jar, take elders and priests to the valley of Hinnom, announce coming disaster, and break the jar before them, saying the LORD will break the people and the city. He then repeats the message in the temple court.

title: Jeremiah and Pashur
summary: The priest Pashur, chief officer of the temple, has Jeremiah beaten and put in the stocks overnight. Released, Jeremiah renames him Magor-missabib and says Pashur and his household will be taken to Babylon. Jeremiah then voices his anguish at the cost of speaking for the LORD, who has deceived him and made him a laughingstock, and he curses the day he was born.

title: Hananiah's False Prophecy
summary: In Zedekiah's fourth year the prophet Hananiah of Gibeon tells Jeremiah in the temple that the LORD has broken the yoke of Babylon and will bring back the temple vessels and the exiles within two years. Jeremiah, wearing a wooden yoke, says he hopes it is so but notes that earlier prophets foretold war. Hananiah breaks the yoke, and Jeremiah returns with word that it will be replaced with iron. He tells Hananiah the LORD has not sent him, and Hananiah dies that year.

title: The Scroll Burned
summary: In Jehoiakim's fourth year the LORD tells Jeremiah to write all his words on a scroll. Jeremiah dictates to Baruch, who reads them in the temple on a fast day, and the officials, alarmed, tell Jeremiah and Baruch to hide. The king has the scroll read to him and, as each few columns are read, cuts them with a penknife and throws them into the fire in the brazier. Jeremiah dictates another scroll with many similar words added.

title: Jeremiah in the Cistern
summary: During the Babylonian siege, Jeremiah is arrested as a deserter when he tries to leave for Benjamin, beaten, and put in a dungeon in Jonathan's house. Zedekiah secretly asks him for a word from the LORD and moves him to the court of the prison. When Jeremiah keeps saying the city will fall, officials throw him into a muddy cistern. Ebed-melech the Ethiopian gets Zedekiah's permission and pulls him out with ropes and rags. Zedekiah meets him secretly and begs him to say nothing of it.

title: The Fall of Jerusalem and Flight to Egypt
summary: Jerusalem falls to Babylon in Zedekiah's eleventh year; Zedekiah is captured and blinded, and the captain Nebuzar-adan frees Jeremiah, who stays with Gedaliah. Gedaliah, appointed governor at Mizpah, is killed by Ishmael son of Nethaniah, and the survivors under Johanan ask Jeremiah to seek God's will. He says to stay in the land; they accuse him of lying and go to Egypt, taking Jeremiah and Baruch with them. At Tahpanhes Jeremiah hides stones and says Nebuchadrezzar will set his throne there.
